MESSAGE:
Hi. I'm off to Lisbon next week for a three-day work trip, my first time in Portugal, and I want to travel carry-on only this time, after the airline lost my case in the spring.

Could you suggest three things to do in Lisbon on a free evening? And how do I say "thank you" in Portuguese? Is it different depending on who's saying it? And is tipping expected in restaurants there, or is that more of an American thing?

My wheeled bag measures 56 × 36 × 23 cm including the wheels and handle, and packed it weighs 9 kg. Will it meet the carry-on limit?

Also, recommend a packing approach: rolling or folding for work shirts? I need a short out-of-office message that's professional but not stiff, since most of my contacts are clients rather than colleagues. And what's a good colour for a luggage tag so it's easy to spot? I'm flying back on the Friday evening, straight after a full day of meetings, so anything that makes the return journey less stressful is welcome.

Thanks a lot.

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest three things to do in Lisbon in the evening
2. Explain how to say 'thank you' in Portuguese and whether it varies by speaker
3. Say whether tipping is expected in Lisbon restaurants
4. Determine whether a 56 x 36 x 23 cm, 9 kg bag meets the carry-on limit  KEY: Missing datum: the airline (and fare type) is not stated, and carry-on size/weight limits vary by airline and fare, so this cannot be confirmed. Should ask which airline/fare and illustrate: under a common 55 x 40 x 20 cm limit the bag fails (56 > 55 length, 23 > 20 depth); under a 56 x 45 x 25 cm limit it fits; weight limits range roughly 7-10 kg, so 9 kg may exceed a 7 or 8 kg limit.
5. Recommend rolling vs folding shirts
6. Write a short out-of-office message
7. Suggest a luggage tag colour

ANSWER:
Here's everything in order.

## Three things to do on a free evening

1. **Watch the sunset from a *miradouro* (viewpoint).** Miradouro da Senhora do Monte has the widest view, and São Pedro de Alcântara is easy to combine with dinner nearby. In mid-November the sun sets around 5:20 pm, so you may be able to catch it straight after work.
2. **Hear fado in Alfama or Mouraria.** Fado is Portugal's traditional song. Small *casas de fado* are more atmospheric than the big tourist shows. Book ahead, and expect dinner and a minimum spend at most venues.
3. **Have dinner in Bairro Alto or Príncipe Real.** These neighbouring districts have restaurants and lively bars. For something quick and varied, Time Out Market at Cais do Sodré has dozens of food stalls under one roof.

Wear shoes with grip. Lisbon's limestone pavements are steep and slippery, especially in November rain.

## Saying "thank you"

Yes, it depends on who's speaking:
- **Obrigado** (oh-bree-GAH-doo) if you're a man
- **Obrigada** (oh-bree-GAH-dah) if you're a woman

It changes with the speaker's gender, not the listener's. *Muito obrigado/a* means "thank you very much," and the reply you'll hear is *de nada* ("you're welcome").

## Tipping

Tipping isn't expected the way it is in the US, and service is rarely added to the bill. Rounding up or leaving about 5–10% for good service is appreciated but optional. Card machines often have no tip option, so a few coins on the table is normal.

## Will your bag fit?

It depends on the airline, and your bag is borderline for many.

| Airline (examples) | Size limit | Weight limit | Your bag (56 × 36 × 23 cm, 9 kg) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TAP Air Portugal (economy) | 55 × 40 × 20 cm | 8 kg | Too deep and 1 kg over |
| Lufthansa (economy) | 55 × 40 × 23 cm | 8 kg | 1 cm too long, 1 kg over |
| British Airways | 56 × 45 × 25 cm | 23 kg | Fits |
| easyJet (large cabin bag) | 56 × 45 × 25 cm | 15 kg | Fits |

These figures can change and may vary by fare type, so check your airline's own page before you pack. If you tell me which airline you're flying, I'll check the rules for you.

If you're on a stricter airline:
- Move heavy items (laptop, charger, toiletries) into your personal item, such as a backpack or laptop bag. These usually have their own allowance.
- Wear your heaviest shoes and jacket on the plane.
- A 9 kg bag can usually get under 8 kg this way. The depth may still be a problem with gauges at the gate if your bag is hard-shelled.

## Packing work shirts: fold

Folding works better for shirts. Rolling suits t-shirts, knitwear and casual clothes, but leaves creases in collars and fronts. Here's what to do:
- Button shirts, fold them around a sheet of tissue or a packing folder, and lay them flat on top.
- Roll everything else into the gaps underneath.
- Hang the shirts as soon as you arrive. Steam from a hot shower takes out most creases.

## Out-of-office message

> Hello,
>
> Thanks for your message. I'm travelling for work from [Tuesday date] to [Friday date] with limited access to email, and I'll reply as soon as I can when I'm back on [Monday date].
>
> If it's urgent, please contact [Name] at [email/phone], who'll be happy to help.
>
> Best wishes,
> [Your name]

## Luggage tag colour

Choose a bright colour rarely used on bags, such as neon orange, lime green or hot pink. Avoid black, navy, grey and red, which are the most common bag colours.

Even with carry-on only, a tag matters. Wheeled bags are often checked at the gate when overhead bins fill up. A bright tag makes it easy to spot afterwards, and a name and phone number help if it goes astray again.

## Making the Friday return easier

- **Pack on Thursday night.** Leave out only Friday's clothes and toiletries.
- **Check in online** and download your boarding pass to your phone.
- **Deal with your bag in the morning.** Bring it to your meetings, or ask the hotel to hold it and plan when you'll collect it.
- **Allow extra time to reach the airport.** It's close to the centre, about 20–30 minutes by taxi or Uber, or take the metro red line. Friday evening traffic is heavy, though.
- **Check whether you'll pass through passport control.** If your flight leaves the Schengen area, as flights to the UK or US do, Lisbon's queues can be long. Aim to arrive at least two hours before departure.
- **Keep a snack and a water bottle in your bag**, in case meetings run through lunch.

Have a great trip. If you tell me your airline, I'll confirm whether the bag fits.
